changes: The call put a number on the next step: 'one or two' more power projects by year-end, with larger scale, longer terms and 'high quality counterparties'. Signed capacity is still 2,588 MW.

Year-end leverage is now about 3.75x before new power projects, leaving about $2bn of room to the 4x ceiling (per CFO). Our preview carried about 3.9x from the 2Q call (transcript not held this run); the basis may differ [INFERENCE].
About $5.9bn of equipment commitments for potential projects surfaced in the 10-Q. The CFO said some carry cancellation terms and declined to tie them to the 6 GW-plus opportunity set.
Partner pricing has 'moved a bit' from the 6.35% of the July Blackstone deal with 10-year Treasuries, per the CFO, who gave no direction; we read it as higher [INFERENCE].
NESE: the Third Circuit remanded the New Jersey certificate. The CEO said this could threaten in-service by next winter, with no material effect on the financial outlook.
checks: Post-call rerun of the 3 November pre-call report, using the Motley Fool, Investing.com and MarketBeat versions of the call (read through a fetch tool that summarizes; several speakers are mislabeled in the Fool text, and direct quotes come from Investing.com or MarketBeat). Figures from the 3Q release and 10-Q carried from the pre-call report, which a fresh subagent checked on 3 November. Derived numbers recomputed in Python. Benzinga and GuruFocus transcripts not readable. A fresh subagent rechecked the draft on 4 November (about 170 figures across the three reports); corrections applied. Not checked: the 10-Q itself, so $5.9bn and 10% to 16% rest on the call; 2Q capex basis unreconciled.
consensus_thesis: Investors own Williams as a fee-based gas pipeline compounder with contracted growth of 11%-plus a year through 2030, and Power Innovation (behind-the-meter generation for hyperscalers) as the AI option on top.
headline: The consensus view does not need to change: the pipeline engine and credit hold, and the AI option gets a dated test (one or two projects by year-end), but its returns are still undisclosed and partner capital may cost more than in July.
kona: Two points for Kona. First, Williams pays for equipment ahead of signed projects at scale, about $5.9bn, and hyperscalers reward speed; Kona should fix turbine or genset slots only with cancellation terms it can state to lenders. Second, the price of partner capital moved within four months of 6.35%, so Kona should not model a fixed JV return; ask infrastructure investors for a range and a rate reset. No change to pricing, since Williams still discloses no PPA price.
monitor: One or two power awards by 31 December: GW, tenor, counterparty, funding structure.
Year-end leverage against about 3.75x, and how new projects use the $2bn of room.
NESE: New Jersey remand, the 9 November Senate cloture vote, in-service date.

sections.body: Emphasized more: Customer quality and tenor on power projects; phased, larger projects; gas-supply security in site choice; partner capital. Emphasized less or dropped: Socrates economics stayed undisclosed; no project-level EBITDA. The 2026-27 leverage squeeze was framed as temporary, with earnings stronger from 2028. KPIs more important: Signed GW, leverage on a stated definition, distributions to Blackstone. Less important: quarterly marketing EBITDA. Risks: Up: NESE timing, cost of JV capital, equipment commitments. Down: Socrates delivery, with Phase 2 due later this week, ahead of schedule and within budget per the CEO. The release called Socrates fully online and also had Plato North on track for mid-November; the call says Phase 2 is still to come.

sections.body: Watch-list: no analyst named by CK; I chose Spiro Dounis (Citi), who pressed hardest on funding. 3Q question: what reaches the high end of the 10% to 16% CAGR he read in the 10-Q, how funding ranks, and how $5.9bn of equipment ties to 6 GW-plus. Answer: 3.5x to 4x target, bolt-ons, partner capital; no strong link between equipment and GW. Rating: partial to deflected. Later evidence: the year-end award and its funding. Also Robert Catellier (CIBC) on JV structure: direct, with pricing moved from 6.35%. No one asked for Socrates EBITDA or agency treatment of the JV. Only the 3Q transcript was held, so the 2Q column is thin. — Trevor
